resources.string: Sleevesight reads what a player says it is playing (track, artist, album). It does not receive the audio or your other notifications. Android grants this with notification access. To find your music players, Sleevesight looks at apps that report what they play (playing or paused) and checks whether it is music (a track with a title and an artist); it stops checking an app for music once it has found some, until Sleevesight starts afresh (not each time you open it). A new player is added to this list switched off. Sleevesight does not follow a player that is off: it does not track what the player plays, and keeps or sends none of it. Switch on the players you want Sleevesight to follow. Calls from the phone app, and sessions Android marks as voice calls, are never read.
External services providing information on artists and music.

Sleevesight pulls information about the currently played music from services dedicated to music and from general information sources. Switch on the services you want Sleevesight to get information from.

Sleevesight uses LLMs to process, aggregate, and present information retrieved from sources. Use the settings to specify the model and effort; stronger models and higher effort provide better results at a higher cost. One service at a time; a service switched off keeps its model and effort.
Private API keys enabling external services
Share phone’s name with Type on a computer

Type on a computer lets you type an API key on a computer’s keyboard, sent to the phone over Bluetooth: tap the keyboard icon in a key’s field, with the page below open on the computer. Sharing the name lets the computer list the phone by its Bluetooth name while a session is open, instead of as “Unknown or Unsupported Device”; a name the phone cannot advertise is left out, and the session says so. Anyone nearby scanning for Bluetooth can see the name meanwhile.

Sleevesight uses external services that require authentication via API keys, obtained from each service’s own website. Your keys are stored encrypted on this phone, and each is sent only to its own service.
Sleevesight collects genre information from sources and compiles a short list of representative categories.
Sleevesight collects track, artist, and album information from sources and uses AI to generate readable descriptions based on the sourced evidence.
Listening history, kept on this phone.

Sleevesight keeps information about the tracks you play on this phone (titles, artists, albums, and when they played), to avoid repeating itself within a listening session and to learn which track changes are your skips. Nothing of it leaves the phone.

The phone’s key that sealed your keys has been deleted.

Purge keys removes every saved key from this phone’s storage, and deletes the key in the phone’s Android Keystore that encrypted them. Any copy left in the storage can then never be decrypted again (crypto-erasure). Sleevesight never sent your keys anywhere but to their own services, and never logged them. Purging keys from Sleevesight does not revoke them. You can still use your API keys elsewhere if you keep another copy.
